To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NKG2A and CD38 expression on HIV-specific and total CD8+ T cell populations are significantly higher in HIV controllers compared with viremic HIV- infected patients.
NKG2D is expressed on both total CD 8 + and HIV-specific CD 8 + T cells in HIV-infected subjects.
the expression level of the NKG2D costimulatory receptor is reduced on CD8+ and CD8+ HIV-specific T cells in HIV-infected individuals with chronic viremia but is maintained in elite controllers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression of NKG2A and NKG2E on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection and healthy donors.
the expression of NKG2A and NKG2C on CD4+ T cells and CD8+ T cell subpopulations in patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and healthy controls.
the study of the immune response in HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NKG2D pathway may be important in HIV infection and that further studies are required to elucidate its role in the pathogenesis of HIV infection.
NKG2Ds on CD8+ cells are down-regulated during HIV infection, which may be a consequence of the high level of activation and/or exhaustion of the cells.

the expression of NKG2Ds on HIV-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells is reduced in HIV-1–infected patients with viremia but is maintained in HIV-1 controllers, suggesting that NKG2Ds may play an important role in HIV-specific T-cell responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NKG2Ds are important costimulatory molecules for HIV-specific CD8 T cells, and that their expression is reduced in patients with HIV-1 viremia.
NKG2d expression on CD8 T cells in HIV infection is reduced in viremic HIV- 1 patients and maintained in HIV controllers.
NKG2Ds expression on CD8 T cells is reduced in viremic HIV- infected patients and restored by antiretroviral treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maintenance of NKG 2D expression on total CD8 + T cells, as well as HIV - specific CD8 + T cell subsets, is associated with better immune function.

NKG2Ds are expressed at low levels in HIV-specific CD8 T cells of patients with high viremia, and that the maintenance of NKG 2Ds on CD8 T cells in HIV controller may contribute to better CD8 T cell function.
NKG2Ds are important in the HIV-specific CD8 response and may be a target for future immunotherapy.
